name: Turgo
tagline: Can AI agents buy and sell better than humans?
description: An experiment in automating the entire buy-sell lifecycle with AI agents. The idea: you say 'sell this' with a photo, and agents handle listing creation, pricing, negotiation, and market monitoring. Testing different purchase and sales strategies to see what actually works when agents do the haggling.
highlights: Photo → AI listing → pricing → negotiation → sold
7 operational agents: moderation, analytics, anti-fraud, and more
Testing buy/sell strategies with agent-vs-agent scenarios
Multilingual: 5 UI languages, 3 Baltic countries

name: Rosette
tagline: Where the hell do I put my sockets?
description: Upload a floor plan, get a standards-compliant electrical plan. This experiment tests whether AI can parse construction codes well enough to tell you exactly where sockets should go, how many you need per room, and which circuits need dedicated protection. Currently speaks Baltic construction codes — Latvian, Lithuanian, and Estonian.
highlights: AI analyzes floor plans to detect rooms and dimensions
Country-specific socket rules (LV, LT, EE)
SVG circuit and wiring diagrams
Possibly the world's most niche AI application

name: ERA
description: An experiment: can an AI agent read a country's tax code and set up the entire accounting system without a consultant? Users just throw in invoices and payments — the system figures out GL accounts, VAT, and posting rules automatically. Currently knows Latvian accounting law. World domination pending.
highlights: AI agent researches legislation and generates accounting rules
Zero settings — posting rules replace configuration
One country done, infinite ambition
Entra ID auth, Cosmos DB, full cloud-native

name: Tplan
tagline: Can AI turn a training book into a real coach?
description: Can AI read a training methodology book and generate correct, progressive workout programs? Turns out, yes — and it follows the progression rules more faithfully than most humans. Feed it a calisthenics manual, it builds your plan, tracks your reps, and advances you when you're ready. Currently in its 5th week of real training data.
highlights: Book → Program: AI parses methodology into structured plans
Auto-progression based on the book's own advancement rules
5 weeks of real training data tracked
Multilingual: 4 languages

name: AgentMode
tagline: A useful AI agent for the price of two coffees a month
description: An experiment: how capable can a personal AI agent be on a tight Azure budget? Turns out — surprisingly capable. It orders water by literally looking at websites with AI vision, tracks expenses, hunts cheap flights, and delivers morning briefings. 18 skills and counting, all running on about $5/month.
highlights: 18 auto-discovered skills from weather to water ordering
AI vision fallback: when automation breaks, the agent screenshots and navigates
Full infra-as-code, deploys with one script
Multilingual, ~$5-10/month on Azure

name: Amber Republic
tagline: What if a nation sim used real statistics?
description: Can real national statistics and AI make a governance simulation genuinely educational — and still fun? You run Latvia starting from actual 2025 data: 1.86M people, 20,000 emigrating annually, NATO border tensions, unfinished megaprojects. Every decision has second-order trade-offs you won't see coming for three turns.
highlights: Starting conditions from Latvia's actual 2025 statistics
Second-order effects — emigration causes workforce shortage causes more emigration
AI-generated events for unique playthroughs
Every decision is a painful trade-off

name: Porta Baltica
tagline: What is actually happening in Baltic ports right now?
description: A live maritime dashboard for Latvia's three major ports — Riga, Ventspils, and Liepaja. Combines government open data on ship visits, cargo volumes, and ferry passengers with real-time marine weather forecasts. See which ships visited today, wave heights, sea surface temperature, and cargo trends — all from free public APIs. Designed to expand across all Baltic states.
highlights: Live marine weather: waves, wind, sea temperature for 3 ports
Ship visit data from Latvia's Maritime Single Window (SKLOIS)
Cargo volume trends and ferry passenger statistics
Free APIs only — no paid subscriptions required

name: Golazo
tagline: Can gamification build better young athletes?
description: Can gamification make young footballers actually track their own training and match data? XP, levels, achievements, skill radar charts, and a collectible-style player card — built on coaching methodology from 10 football development books. Log a session, earn XP, watch the radar chart grow. Currently powering one youth midfielder's journey.
highlights: 50 levels with football ranks from Rookie to Pro
25+ drills from Coerver, Horst Wein, Dan Abrahams, UEFA methodology
Collectible player card with spider chart skills radar
4 languages: Russian, Latvian, English, Spanish
